title: Introduce Session Scheduler and Token Curator for Go SDK (parity + ergonomic retry presets)
author: Asha Menon
release_notes: Add Session Scheduler and Token Curator to Go SDK; exposes lightweight ergonomic APIs for coordinated token warmup and retry presets; bump go SDK to v1.9.0. No user-facing breaking changes.
description: Context: Several customers observed credential stampedes and inefficient reauth churn for long-lived streaming sessions. Motivation: provide a Go-native facility that coordinates credential refreshes across concurrent stream handles, prefetches rotation windows, and exposes simple presets so application teams can get safe defaults without custom retry wiring. This PR implements two related pieces: 1) Session Scheduler: a light-weight scheduler that groups imminent token refreshes (TTL windows) and serializes refreshes to a single upstream token provider when safe, with configurable jitter and fanout limits to avoid leader election overhead; 2) Token Curator: a prefetching/validation layer that tracks upcoming rotation windows and primes a hot-swappable cached token to reduce first-byte latency on reauth. Design notes: - Scheduler binds to the SDK's SessionFactory and can be enabled per-client or globally via SessionSchedulerOptions. - Token Curator exposes a minimal interface (Curator.Start, Curator.Stop, Curator.Get) and hooks into the existing CredentialProvider interface for seamless compatibility. - Provides a new RetryPreset: "session-friendly" that adjusts hedged retry bounds for long-lived streams and prefers graceful backoff on auth-failures. - Backwards compatible: default behavior is disabled; existing consumers continue to use the prior credential cache. Checklist: - [x] Implement scheduler and curator in go/sdk/cred - [x] Add unit + integration tests that simulate concurrent stream churn - [x] Add e2e perf harness measuring reauth QPS and tail latency - [x] Add docs and examples demonstrating enabling via client opts - [x] Version bump to v1.9.0 Implementation summary and notes: The scheduler uses a small, sharded token map keyed by session id and TTL bucket. It performs coordinated refresh by electing a local refresh leader per bucket using an atomic compare-and-swap and falling back to queued refresh so only one outbound token call is made per bucket in the rotation window. The Token Curator keeps a ring of prefetched tokens per identity and validates tokens asynchronously; stale tokens are evicted promptly. Observability: added span annotations and metrics: cred.curator.prefetches, cred.scheduler.leaders, cred.refresh.latency, and a lightweight gauge for cached token age. Compatibility: The PR keeps the public CredentialProvider surface unchanged; new constructs are optional and documented. Migration: recommend enabling the session-friendly preset for services with >100 concurrent streams to reduce auth QPS. Performance: in the perf harness we observed ~3.8x reduction in outbound token calls under a simulated 1k-conn churn pattern and 14% P99 tail latency improvement for stream connect times after enabling curator+scheduler.
